title: Spiral galaxy ESO 269-57
caption: The central region of the spiral galaxy ESO 269-57, imaged by the Very Large Telescope
celestial: ESO 269-57 · constellation Centaurus · about 150 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This photo shows the central region of the spiral galaxy ESO 269-57, about 150 million light-years away in the southern constellation Centaurus. Its bright centre is overexposed here, and it is surrounded by a ring, a feature built into its classification.

Astronomers label it type Sar, with the "r" standing for that ring. Around the galaxy, many other galaxies at about the same distance form a loose cluster, and fainter, more distant galaxies sit in the background.

The name has its own story. It comes from the ESO/Uppsala Survey of the Southern Sky, carried out in the 1970s, which catalogued over 15,000 southern galaxies. The photo itself was made with KUEYEN, one of the telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope, combining three exposures in blue, yellow-green and red light, of 600, 300 and 300 seconds.
scale: The source lists a distance of 150 million light years, so the light in this picture set out roughly 150 million years ago.

understand.summary: This composite was made with the KUEYEN telescope of the VLT from blue, yellow-green and red exposures. The packet does not publish which colour was assigned to each exposure.
understand.eye: The galaxy is far too faint to see this way without a large telescope; the exposures gather much more light than an eye can.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: The image quality is 0.7 arcseconds and the field covers 90 by 90 arcseconds, with north up and east to the left.
alt: The bright, overexposed centre of a spiral galaxy surrounded by a ring, with other galaxies in the field.
